name: MO-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Open seat after Sam Graves' retirement
Republican candidate has far outraised the Democrat
Prediction markets price the race at 94% Republican
model.rationale: The district's R+19 lean and an open-seat dynamic point firmly to Republicans, and Chris Stigall's fundraising edge over Josh Smead reinforces that. Prediction markets price Republican chances around 94%, consistent with a Safe R rating despite the absence of polls.
model.watch: A late Democratic fundraising surge or outside spending could narrow the margin, though a win would require an exceptional environment shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northwest Missouri's sixth district is a deeply Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about nineteen points toward the GOP. Sam Graves is retiring, so this is an open-seat contest rather than a race against an entrenched incumbent, which removes one Republican advantage but does little to change the underlying terrain.

Republican Chris Stigall has raised roughly $600,000, far outpacing Democrat Josh Smead's $72,000, and prediction markets give Republicans about a 94% chance of holding the seat. With no public polling and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Republican hold in the mid-to-high teens.
